title: The Boy From Block 66: A WW2 Jewish Holocaust Survival True Story
series: Heroic Children of World War II Book 1
author: Limor Regev
target_audience: Readers interested in Holocaust survivor narratives
Students and scholars of World War II history
Jewish community and those interested in Jewish heritage
Readers seeking inspirational and true life stories
General adults and mature teens (due to subject matter)
core_themes: The brutality and resilience witnessed during the Holocaust
Hope, humanity, and the strength of the human spirit
Family bonds and friendship in adversity
Historical remembrance and the importance of testimony
primary_purpose: To bear witness to the Holocaust through the personal journey of Sami Steigmann—a Jewish boy who survived Auschwitz and other horrors—preserving history and imparting lessons of resilience, courage, and hope for future generations.

structure_format.organization: Divided into sections/chapters that follow Sami’s journey; includes pre-war childhood, the Holocaust period (ghettos, camps, Block 66), and post-war aftermath
features: First-person and third-person perspectives based on survivor's testimony

key_concepts_lessons: Personal stories illuminate the human cost of genocide and hate.
Even amidst atrocity, courage and kindness exist—sometimes in the smallest acts.
The preservation of memory and testimony is critical to preventing future atrocities.
Childhood experiences in war irrevocably shape survivors’ lives.
The resilience of the human spirit enables survival, but the scars endure.
Every survivor’s story is unique and valuable to our collective history.
style_tone: Unflinching in recounting trauma but uplifting in perseverance
notable_features: Based on the real-life story of Sami Steigmann, a child survivor of Auschwitz
Highlights Block 66—an area of Buchenwald concentration camp dedicated to housing children
Personalizes the Holocaust through one boy’s lens, providing emotional insight
Combines vivid storytelling with historical context
Part of a larger series documenting children’s survival during WWII
cultural_historical_context: The book is set during the Holocaust (1940s Europe), with post-war reflections. Published in the 21st century, it contributes to Holocaust education as firsthand survivors age. The story both memorializes the suffering of over one million Jewish children and educates a new generation about the dangers of hatred, antisemitism, and indifference.
reception_impact: Widely praised for its honest and poignant depiction of Holocaust survival
Used in educational settings for Holocaust and WWII studies
Appreciated for its accessibility to general readers as well as historians
Regarded as an essential addition to Holocaust memoir literature
Promotes empathy and awareness about one of history’s darkest periods
comparable_titles: Survivors Club: The True Story of a Very Young Prisoner of Auschwitz by Michael Bornstein and Debbie Bornstein Holinstat
The Boy on the Wooden Box by Leon Leyson
Man's Search for Meaning by Viktor E. Frankl
